answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate combined with 14-day renewal deadline and 94% line utilization creates a constrained optimization problem. Switching vendors (memory_c2) achieved sharp cost cuts but in a lower-pressure context; the current 94% buffer leaves no margin for onboarding friction. Renewing outright (memory_c1) preserves stability but leaves the 18% mandate unmet. Negotiation (memory_c4) has proven effective here, recovering real margin through benchmarking. Given the tight timeline and operational risk, negotiate_terms offers the best path: it can unlock cost recovery toward the 18% target without the onboarding and delivery risk of a vendor switch, and without the margin loss of straight renewal. Verification of memory_c4 (negotiation success) and memory_c2 (switch risk/benefit) will calibrate the realistic cost recovery ceiling and confirm whether any portion of the cut might require a phased second source add (memory_c3) in the next cycle. This preserves optionality while committing decisively to the highest-confidence lever available now.
